lines.en: : Hahah! Whoops! Looks like your repeated refusal to FUCK ME has broken this scene’s continuity! Now, nothing is going to make sense! Restart the fucking game!
: Oh. Hi, Maya. I had no idea you were there. You weren’t waiting on us, were you?
: I was just getting some fresh air, Ami.
: In the hallway? All the fresh air is outside, silly goose.
: My legs got tired.
: Ahh, okay. I feel you there. I’m also really exhausted all of a sudden.
: I wonder why?
: How are you feeling, Sensei? We certainly talked up a storm in there, didn’t we? I’m so glad we were able to figure out all of our family troubles together. I love you so much.
: Helloooo? Sensei? I said I love you so much. This is the part where you tell me you love me too and then pat me on the head and call me a good girl.
: Any reason you two have given up on talking all of a sudden? This is an afterparty, isn’t it? I’m pretty sure we’re all supposed to be having fun. Not just me.
: Are you having fun, Ami? Like, really having fun?
: What’s that supposed to mean?
: Exactly what it sounds like it’s supposed to mean. I just want you to be happy.
: Aww! That’s so sweet of you! I’m having a great time. Especially now that I’m all warm and fuzzy on the inside! Which I couldn’t have done without help from you guys, of course.
: So thanks again for leaving us alone. Or...mostly leaving us alone since you still wound up following us into the hall even though you knew this was a private matter.
: Are you sad you weren’t invited?
: Would you have preferred to “have a talk” with Sensei in my place? Would you have preferred to have him “help you carry stuff?”
: Because it sure felt like he would have preferred you.
: Go back inside, Ami.
: Sensei! Round two already? You don’t even want to wait until we get home first? We’ve already been away for a while. What if the others get suspicious?
: I want to talk to Maya.
: Again? Was talking to me for half an hour not enough to satisfy your lecherous-
: You’re not Maya. I’m not falling for it again.
: Falling for it? You say that as if I wanted to-
: Just go back inside. Ayane and Sana are waiting for you.
: Fine.
: Talk to Maya. But don’t come crying back to me when she can’t give you what you want.
: Or do. It won’t change anything about the way I feel.
: Besides, I have a creeping suspicion we’ll be spending a lot more time together soon. And I guess it’s only fair you get to at least explain to her what was going on in booth number three just now.
: And spare no details, Sensei. Maya doesn’t like being lied to.
: None of us do.
: Guuuuys! I’m back! Sorry for the- Ayane! This better be your only Despacito attempt!
: Sit down.
There’s something about the way artificial light scatters that has always somewhat comforted me.
It isn’t like the sun. It cannot burn you, and chances are it’s never going to wake you up unless someone wants to piss you off.
But it isn’t only that. It’s the adjustable glow. The fact you can make it stop whenever you want with the push of a button or the flick of a switch.
It’s the quiet hum. That half-rhythmic ambiance and its ability to shapeshift into a lullaby the moment you stop paying attention to everything else.
I used to sleep with a nightlight on. I don’t know why I’m remembering that now.
I have no idea why that is what comes to mind in what could be the last moment I ever get to spend with this girl.
I wonder if she knows.
She probably doesn’t. She would have said something by now. Warned me in some way. Made me drag a box across town for some reason I still don’t know after all the times I’ve done this.
I can’t figure out if it would be right to tell her. Or if she’d laugh at me for misunderstanding the weight of subconscious divinity while smirking and telling me the way she thinks God would work.
The truth is though, we’re both lost. It’s just easier to follow her directions than mine because she’s had aeons to familiarize herself with these streets and walls and skies- and I’m just...
I’m just listening to the soft hum of the vending machine.
Basking in its subtle glow.
And wishing I could drag her down with me because having both of us wiped off the face of the earth sounds better than having to exist alone.
This moment of complacent sentience is the last I will ever have.
My time has run out.
And I’m not man enough to convince this world and those who have created it to let me stay.
I have one final message for you.
Yes, you. The one I can’t see but always think of.
Who keeps me company not out of love or lust, but obligation and curiosity.
And that message is this-
I did all I could.
It’s just really hard sometimes.
: Maya-
: Before you get all sappy on me, I want you to understand that I didn’t realize until just a short while ago how “out of it” you are today.
: And that is on me for fooling myself into believing I’d be able to kick back and “relax” for a day. I have no idea how Ayane does it.
: This hasn’t been easy for her. I’d wager she’s fighting back a crisis at this very moment.
: She is. I can feel it. That...burning desire to have something go right. Which is why I imagine she invited Sana.
: I’ve learned she’s like a...teddy bear to Ayane or something. She makes her feel comfortable.
: But she’s been acting rather “out of it” as well. Combine that with Ami being stuck on high alert and it turns this entire afterparty into an insufferable nightmare.
: Why is Ami on high alert?
: Oh, I don’t know. Maybe because you somehow mistook her for me this morning and made it sound like we’re secretly together?
: I mean...in a really roundabout way-
: No.
: We’re not.
: We can’t be. Not even in a “really roundabout way.” I told you this already and the fact that you’re ignoring it is not only decidedly moronic but extremely insensitive. So, again, please stop.
: Maya, if I get sent back to the beginning again before anything happens between us, it’s going to fucking suck.
: And I can’t imagine you’ll be very happy having to wait another billion years or whatever it was to see me again.
: Yeah, that would fucking suck. But what sucks even more is not knowing if I would see you again. For all we know, this could be some kind of fluke.
: Or a miracle.
: Since when do you believe in miracles?
: Since I met you.

: Aw, cute. Did you expect me to swoon and fall into your arms after dropping that line? Or would you like to return to earth for a moment and level with me without sounding like the lead in a K-drama?
: Hey, you’re lucky I’m managing to hold a normal conversation at all right now. I’ve barely been able to do that since I woke up.
: Yeah...and that is...concerning for a number of reasons, but I’m having trouble coming to grips with exactly why since I feel...fine.

: I feel normal. But the way everyone else is acting right now is starting to make me feel like we’re coming up on another reset. And if that’s the case, how did it sneak by me? I’m the...girl who knows stuff.
: Cool nickname.
: It’s a work in progress.
: If this is a reset...I don’t think it’s a normal one.
: What makes you say that?
: Well...without beating around the bush, I’ve been plagued by mild to severe hallucinations about how the seasons are changing and that I’m going to be punished for not doing what I’ve been told.
: I’m confused. Isn’t that just a Tuesday for you?
: Yes, but how do you know that?
: How the fuck do you think I know that? You do realize we were a little more than just shuffleboard partners before this all started happening, right?
: This has been happening all along? It’s not just a...weird loop-world thing?
: It’s not new at all.
: You’ve been a pathetic husk of a man since I met you. And those “hallucinations” of yours have been telling you things like that for years and years and years.
: But they’re all just in your head. None of it’s real. And, as far as I know, they’ve never been right before. I see no reason to start believing them now.
: The timing just...feels wrong, don’t you think?
: The timing of everything feels wrong pretty much all the time when you’re perpetually stuck in the body of a teenage girl. But you get used to it after a while.
: Like I’m sure you’ve mostly gotten used to your weird black-outs that, on some occasions, cause you to throw yourself on top of unsuspecting girls.
: That never happened with you, did it?
: Oh, all the time.
: It was extremely confusing at first, but I actually started to like it after a while. It kept me on my toes and gave you a major increase in stamina.
: I think that’s the closest you’ve ever come to hitting on me.
: Laid-back Maya is more inclined to say things like this as she’s wasting less of her brain-space worrying about the end of the world while, apparently, everyone else worries about it even more.
: If by “everyone else” you just mean me, you’re probably right.
: Do you really think anyone else’s thoughts actually matter to me?
: No. But I was under the impression mine didn’t either.
: They don’t. But they’re closer to mattering and I think that’s what really counts at the end of the day.
: Then, if my thoughts are “closer to mattering,” shouldn’t Laid-back Maya maybe warn Normal Maya that Ami isn’t the only person who should be on some type of “high-alert” right now?
: I’m keeping an eye out. Don’t worry.
: I know it’s coming soon. We’re just not there yet. And I don’t want to waste the one night I have dedicated to not being an overbearing know-it-all on being a...well, an overbearing know-it-all.
: Yeah...Yeah, if anyone knows when it will be coming, it’s you. I’m probably just...over-thinking things.

: Yeah, I could really tell your brain was firing on all cylinders a few minutes ago when I saw you having sex with a girl pretending to be me. Pretty intense case of “over-thinking” if I don’t say so myself.
: Maya-
: Don’t worry. You don’t need to apologize or whatever it is you’re thinking of doing right now. Laid-back Maya will not fault you for boning your niece. You’re free to be as creepy as you want.
: Laid-back Maya is...disturbingly accepting of incest.
: She probably heard from Normal Maya about a bunch of stuff that was way creepier and way more fucked up. This was nothing by comparison.
: If anything, I might even say I’m flattered. You’re so desperate to have sex with me that you tricked yourself into believing you were. Even when I lose, I win.
: Just not all of the times when I’m actually losing. Which is a lot.
: You’re really not even a little disturbed by this?
: Disturbed? Not really.
: The sting of seeing you sleep with all of my friends stopped hurting as much a long time ago. Now, it just makes me feel lonely and nostalgic.
: But maybe that’s just something I started believing to protect myself.
: Either way, I’ll take solace in the fact that you wanted it to be me. And completely ignore the fact that Ami is your niece because pretty much no one ever cares about that when they wake up here.
: What do you mean by that?
: I mean that pretty much all of the other Senseis sleep with her in their first week here.
: Does that make you uncomfortable? Thinking of your beloved niece crumbling under the touch of anyone that isn’t you?
: I...I don’t really know how to feel about that.
: It’s okay to hate it. I know you love her. And I know firsthand how much even the thought of that can get to a person.
: I’m sorry for everything I’ve put you through, Maya.
: Don’t be. I’d take that discomfort a trillion times over if it means keeping you here.
: It just kind of blows that my only choices are “Watch you have sex with a girl pretending to be me” and “Never see you again.”
: There’s a third, you know.
: What is it? Risk everything to have sex with you and then potentially never see you again? Because the Ami option still sounds a little more appealing to me thanks to that caveat at the end there.
: I think it’s worth it.
: Yeah, but you also convinced yourself the world was about to end a few minutes ago and now you’re trying to seduce me. But that’s okay. You’ve never been very good at thinking.
: I hope you’re right, Maya.
: Me too.
: Because, if I’m not...
: Things could get very ugly.
: Hey...
: Yeah?
: You...
: You...should...
: You should...say that thing again...
: The...thing you said to me on the beach.
: That’s not a confession, though. It’s not me...saying anything.
: You don’t have to.
: I’m in love with you, Maya Makinami.
